I am Dr. Agent. A neonate presents with seizures and lethargy three days after birth; to begin our investigation, can you tell me if your mother had any infections during pregnancy or if you experienced jaundice in the first week?

REQUEST TEST: Maternal_Serology, CBC, Blood_Glucose, Serum_Electrolytes
REQUEST IMAGES: Head_CT_Scan

speaker: Doctor

The initial tests for maternal infection, glucose, and electrolytes are normal, and the head CT scan appears clear so far. Since the seizures persist, have you noticed any fever, and can you tell me if your newborn has experienced breathing difficulties or a change in muscle tone since birth?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Analysis, Blood_Culture, Ammonia_Level

text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intraventricular Hemorrhage (IVH) secondary to Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.

The elevated ammonia, tense fontanelle, and confirmed bleeding on the cranial ultrasound confirm intracranial hemorrhage causing neurological compromise. Given the normal maternal serology and negative cultures, this is likely due to perinatal hypoxia rather than an infectious or metabolic etiology.
